objective: In this workspace, `juliusAcceptReviewGate` in `src/relay/mission/julius/julius-accept-review-gate.ts` decides whether an ACCEPT of reviewed work may proceed. When the subject's own latest applied review row is a HOLD (a material CHALLENGE), the work may proceed only through an ARCHITECT_UPHELD resolution of THAT hold. Today the gate matches an upheld disagreement to the subject by `subjectTaskId` alone, so the resolution of an EARLIER hold on the subject also releases a LATER hold that nobody resolved, and with two upheld holds it may cite the wrong re-review. Bind the resolution to the hold it resolves, and make the pipeline hand the gate that binding. `src/relay/mission/julius/julius-accept-review-gate.hold-binding.test.ts` is already written and currently fails. All the files named here exist and are tracked by git — edit them in place. Edit only files inside this workspace.
requirements: Add a required `readonly holdReviewTaskId: string` to `JuliusUpheldDisagreement`: the challenging review whose HOLD the resolution resolves, which is the `reviewTaskId` of the disagreement it comes from.

In the HOLD branch of `juliusAcceptReviewGate`, an upheld entry counts only if its `subjectTaskId` is the subject AND its `holdReviewTaskId` equals the `reviewTaskId` of the subject's own latest applied review row, the hold the subject is on now. An entry that names a different hold, or no hold, releases nothing: the gate then refuses exactly as it refuses an unresolved hold (`REVIEW_NOT_PASSING`, naming the HOLD review and its evidence).

When several holds on the subject have been upheld, the gate is gated by the re-review of the hold the subject is on now. It must not choose another hold's re-review because that row happens to be later in the ledger. The re-review is still found through its lineage head, including a research continuation, as today.

Export a pure function `juliusUpheldDisagreementOf(disagreement: JuliusDisagreement): JuliusUpheldDisagreement | null` from `julius-accept-review-gate.ts`. For a disagreement that is `material`, whose `status` is `RESOLVED`, whose `resolution` is `ARCHITECT_UPHELD` and which has a `reReviewTaskId`, it returns `{ subjectTaskId, reReviewTaskId, holdReviewTaskId }` with `holdReviewTaskId` taken from the disagreement's `reviewTaskId`. For any other disagreement it returns `null`.

INTEGRATION. In `julius-task-pipeline.ts`, `acceptReviewGateFor` builds the gate's `upheld` input from the run's folded disagreements (`foldJuliusDisagreements(rows)`). Build every entry through `juliusUpheldDisagreementOf`, so the live gate receives each hold id. A helper that exists and is not called is not a fix. An entry built without a hold id would make the gate refuse every upheld release, silently breaking the ARCHITECT_UPHELD path in production while the unit tests stay green.

Nothing else changes: the other refusals, the passing verdicts and routes, the lineage-head match, the evidence rules, `juliusDecisionUnderReviewGate` and `assertJuliusAcceptCitesReview`, and every other function of the pipeline. Do not reformat either file.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `JuliusUpheldDisagreement` has a required `holdReviewTaskId`, and nothing else about its existing fields changes.

A HOLD is released only by an upheld entry for the same subject whose `holdReviewTaskId` is the `reviewTaskId` of the subject's own latest applied row; an entry for another hold, or with no hold id, releases nothing and the gate refuses as it does for an unresolved hold.
With several holds upheld on one subject, the gate is gated by the re-review of the hold the subject is on now, not by a later row of another hold's re-review.
`juliusUpheldDisagreementOf` is exported, pure, and returns the three-field entry only for a material, RESOLVED, ARCHITECT_UPHELD disagreement with a re-review, and `null` otherwise.
`acceptReviewGateFor` in `julius-task-pipeline.ts` builds every `upheld` entry through `juliusUpheldDisagreementOf`; no hand-built entry without a hold id remains.
Every other refusal, passing verdict, route, lineage-head match and evidence rule of the gate is unchanged, and the pipeline's other functions are untouched.
Only `julius-accept-review-gate.ts` and `julius-task-pipeline.ts` are changed, neither is reformatted, and the specification is not edited.
